correctness.rationale: The orthogonal Laurent basis gives the m-step weighted shift and diagonal a_n=I_{n+m}/I_n−I_n/I_{n−m}. Strict moment log-convexity gives positivity and injectivity. Writing k=n+1, the positive-index difference is m²/[k(k+m)] up to exponentially small errors at fixed r; at negative infinity the same leading rational term is multiplied by r^{2m}. The tails give the claimed combined sorting coefficient, compactness and cutoff p>1/2; telescoping by residue class gives m(1−r^{2m}). With h=mε and y=ε(n+1), the exponent difference is bounded by the triangular average of L''=Θ because −2<L'<0. On compact windows a_n/h²→Θ uniformly, and the global bound by a constant times (1+y²)^{−1} establishes summable mesh tails exactly when p>1/2. Strict decrease of Θ follows from sinh³ y>y³ cosh y by the power series (coefficients coincide in degrees 3 and 5 and are larger on the left in all higher odd degrees). Thus Θ≤1/3, the norm is attained asymptotically at y=0, and positive-level counts converge by the zero measure of the level boundary; at and above 1/3 the strict-threshold count is already zero. For the quadratic constant, the differentiated Euler product terms 2(a²−y²)/(a²+y²)², a=πk, have summable L² norms proportional to a^{−3/2}. This justifies termwise Fourier transformation in L² without an unjustified absolute L¹ interchange. The transforms sum to 2π|ξ|/(exp(π|ξ|)−1), and Plancherel gives the stated 8(ζ(2)−ζ(3))/π² before the m⁴ factor. The finite checker was inspected; the analytic arguments establish the infinite claims.
